info.description:
The director's API of the Floor42 daemon, on loopback only (ADR-0007). Every route under /api needs the session token except /api/status: the browser sends its session cookie (and `X-Floor42-Request: 1` on every change, with its own Origin); a script sends a script token issued from the desk (System > Sessions and tokens, ADR-0044) as a bearer, limited to its scope.

```
# a script token issued from the desk, shown once (scope read, missions:write or all; at most 30 days)
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLOOR42_TOKEN" http://127.0.0.1:7420/api/missions
```

`FLOOR42_DIRECTOR_TOKEN_FILE=true` (writing the director's token to `~/.floor42/session.token`) still works but is deprecated: unconfined agents can read that file. A request a proxy forwarded (`X-Forwarded-For`, `X-Forwarded-Host`, `Forwarded`) is refused with `FORWARDED`: reach a remote daemon through an SSH tunnel (docs/remote.md).

Identifiers are short and readable: missions M-1, tickets T-1, questions Q-1, lessons L-1, notes N-1; agents are named (geoffrey, chris). Every error comes back as `{"code": "...", "message": "..."}`, with a stable code: 400 when the request itself is wrong (`INVALID_ARGUMENT`, `MISSING_...`, `BAD_REQUEST` for a body that cannot be read), 401 without the session token (`UNAUTHORIZED`), 403 from another host or origin (`FORBIDDEN`), 404 when what it names does not exist (`NOT_FOUND`), 409 when the state of things refuses it (a business rule), 413 when it is too large, 503 when the journal cannot be written (`JOURNAL_UNAVAILABLE`). Every fact is recorded in the journal with its origin (REAL or SIMULATED): what the API returns is rebuilt from it.

## Authentication

Three schemes, applied per path group. `cookieAuth`: the browser's sign-in cookie, plus `X-Floor42-Request: 1` on every request that changes something and an `Origin` that is exactly the daemon's own. `bearerToken`: a script token with scope `read` (reads only), `missions:write` (reads, plus the MISSION_WRITES allow-list: create a mission, approve or reject it and its tickets, nudge it, send a workshop directive, answer a question that is not a permission) or `all`; it needs neither the header nor an Origin. `agentBearer`: an agent session's hook credential, accepted on `/hooks/*` and `/mcp` only and refused with 403 on `/api`. `/api/status` is open. The sign-in link request (`POST /auth/open`, outside this document) answers 429 `TOO_MANY_REQUESTS` when one was just opened.

## Stability

The stable core is every route not marked `x-stability: unstable`. Unstable routes (identity, calls, demo, terminals, plugins, sandbox, backups, resume, projects, workflows, committee roles, lessons, some mission helpers, the journal helpers, `/mcp`, `/hooks/*`) may change in any release, with no notice. A change to the stable core is listed in the changelog.

## Status codes

Every success is `200`, creates and deletes included: there is no `201` or `204`, by decision. Errors are the shared responses of this document, all with the `Problem` body.

## Idempotency

`POST /api/missions` accepts an `Idempotency-Key` header: the same request sent twice with one key creates one mission.

post.description: Asks the dispatcher to look at the mission again, as it does after each event it knows: work that can run starts. Nothing is forced; returns the progress of every mission.

The director objects at acceptance (ADR-0060): 1 to 10 `objections`, each of 1 to 4 000 characters, in one command and one journal transaction. An objection with a `ticket` (a done work ticket of the mission) reopens it with the text as a directive: its producer resumes in its own worktree, then its review and the mission's checks run again. An objection without `ticket` is new work: a work ticket the director creates (approved), with the criterion `Done as the director's objection asks: <text>`, under the mission's permission table only. The events of one round share the cause `objections-<n>`; the report groups them. The mission must wait for the acceptance (409 `NOT_AT_ACCEPTANCE`: in progress, every ticket done or dropped). Also refused: 409 `PROOF_RUNNING` while the proof runs, 409 `CLOSING` while the mission closes, 409 `AGENT_AT_WORK` while an agent works on it, 409 `NO_PRODUCTION_IN_WORKFLOW` for new work on a workflow that produces nothing, 409 `INVALID_TRANSITION` for a ticket that is not a done work ticket. A refusal records nothing. The proof of the delivery becomes stale once the code changes, and the acceptance asks again. Answers the mission.

Nothing runs and nothing is recorded.

post.description: Starts Floor42's steps of every recipe (ADR-0058) and answers at once (`running` true); follow it with `GET /proof`. Each producer must be idle (409 `WORKTREE_BUSY`) and the mission not closing (409 `CLOSING`); they stay held until the run ends. Each worktree is copied into a folder Floor42 owns and the steps run on the copy, in the WSL sandbox with the network cut, never on the host and never in the worktree; the copy is deleted afterwards without following any link or junction in it. Files git lists that cannot be copied (links, names outside the worktree or Windows cannot hold, colliding cases) are left out and named in `skipped` with their reason; the size cap (500 MiB, 20 000 files) is checked before anything is copied. Each step stops at `floor42.proof.step-timeout-seconds`; its output keeps its last 8 000 characters; a recipe stops at its first failed step. Each run is journaled (`ProofRan`, by Floor42, with the recipe digest, the commit and the digest of the uncommitted work). Refused with 409 `SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE`, `NOTHING_TO_RUN` or `PROOF_RUNNING`.

Its review starts again after the fix. No new ticket and no new mission. Refused with 409 `NOTHING_TO_SEND_BACK` when nothing failed and no note is given, and as a directive would be (a closed mission). Answers the ticket's id.

Every figure carries its `basis`: `MEASURED` (Floor42's clock and check runs, git read now), `ESTIMATED` (cost: Claude Code's estimate, not a bill; null when no session reported one), `REPORTED` (an agent's words). `outputs` lists, per worktree with its absolute path, the commits beyond the project's branch, the files not committed and the files git ignores (50 named, all counted): those are in no commit, so no merge or pull request carries them. `warnings` says so first. `next` gives each next step (CLOSE, REOPEN, PULL_REQUEST, MERGE, FOLLOW_UP, ARCHIVE) with the refusal it would meet now; `followUp` prefills a follow-up mission.
